a_css.root_cause: A (www.growmax.io / Replit) is the frozen pre-migration build. package.json diff between commit 5c2a864 (last package.json/lockfile change before the Next.js migration) and d8c8b05 (P2.4, the deployed commit) shows the entire toolchain was replaced: build tool moved from Vite+esbuild+wouter+Express (using the '@tailwindcss/vite' plugin) to Next.js App Router (using '@tailwindcss/postcss' + autoprefixer); scripts changed from 'vite dev'/'tsx script/build.ts' to 'next dev --turbopack'/'next build'. Both sides pin the SAME tailwindcss/postcss/next core versions within the migration branch (ruling out a simple dependency-bump regression), but the underlying component markup was rewritten as part of the framework migration, so Tailwind's JIT content scan legitimately produces a different set of utility classes for the two builds. This is expected fallout of the framework rewrite itself, not a code or data regression introduced during P5.
a_css.classification: real (different rule sets present/absent), with a portion of the reported per-selector 'differing declaration' noise being benign Tailwind class-grouping artifacts
a_css.visitor_visible_risk: Low but not zero. None of the 291 A-only classes were found in the actual class attributes of the captured homepage or the how-to-migrate-from-tradgecko page HTML (checked directly), meaning the CSS chunk is shared across many routes and these classes belong to OTHER pages/components not exercised by the P5.2 crawl's diff assertions (which only check visibleTextHash/links/assetRefs, not per-element computed style). Recommend a targeted visual diff pass over pages using color-variant badges/tags (e.g. blog category chips, comparison-page accents) before declaring full visual parity; not a blocker for G5 itself since it is a known, explainable framework-rewrite side effect rather than an unexplained regression.

b_tradgecko_link.current_live_recheck: Refetched both pages directly just now: both A and B render the IDENTICAL absolute href 'https://www.growmax.io/contact?utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=tradegecko-alternatives'. The divergence recorded in the P5.2 attempt-1 manifest no longer reproduces.
b_tradgecko_link.db_rows_identical_precondition: P4.3 already proved the blog post row (rich-text body) is byte-identical between source and target, so the differing href could not have come from different stored content.
b_tradgecko_link.rendering_cause: Transient rendering/edge-cache staleness on A at the moment of the P5.2 capture, not a code, data, or link-classification-harness bug specific to this URL. A's blog post route sets 'cache-control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate' at the app layer, but the origin is fronted by Google Frontend/GAE (per the 'server: Google Frontend' / 'via: 1.1 google' response headers seen on every A request), which is known to serve a short-lived stale copy of a dynamically-rendered response for a brief window (consistent with the same GAE-fronted caching behavior documented for A's '/' and '/sitemap.xml' in finding (c) below). By the time this investigation re-fetched the page (~20 minutes after the P5.2 capture), A's rendering had converged to match B's, with no further divergence found.
b_tradgecko_link.related_posts_ruled_out: The other 7 of the 8 URLs in the 'blog_body_internal_link_drift' bucket are fully explained by the harness's isSameSite-vs-capture-origin bug (already documented in P5.2's classification.internalLinks_externalLinks); this URL is the one exception and is now resolved as described above, not a related-posts/created_at-tie issue.

verdict: All three questions answered with direct, re-derived evidence: (a) CSS divergence is real (different Tailwind utility sets), caused by the Vite->Next.js framework rewrite itself with identical pinned dependency versions on both branches -- not a version-drift bug, low visitor-visible risk, worth a follow-up visual pass but not a G5 blocker; (b) the tradgecko-page link divergence was a transient A-side rendering/edge-cache staleness artifact that has since self-resolved and reproduces identically on both sides now; (c) the '/' and '/sitemap.xml' diffs are fully and exclusively explained by A serving stale long-TTL cached pages that predate 9 already-published posts confirmed live in A's own /api/blog, with no residual content gap.
